items.description: The boundary layer (app/routes/) does not import the database session object
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no SQLAlchemy ORM import statements
The service layer (app/services/) contains no SQLAlchemy ORM import statements
Session operations (add, merge, execute, query) are called exclusively from within app/repositories/ and are absent from app/services/ and app/routes/
No hardcoded database connection string appears in any application module
The application reads the database connection URL exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable
The stock_records Alembic migration completes a single-step downgrade followed by a single-step upgrade without error, marked @pytest.mark.migration and never applied against the base revision
Rows seeded into stock_records before the migration is applied are present with all original column values intact after the upgrade completes
The database rejects an INSERT into stock_records where sku is NULL
The database rejects an INSERT into stock_records where location is NULL
The database rejects an INSERT into stock_records where inventory_code is NULL
The database rejects an INSERT into stock_records where quantity is NULL
The database CHECK constraint rejects a direct INSERT into stock_records with quantity less than zero, verified against the real branch database
The service layer raises a rejection error when a request to file a stock record carries a negative quantity value, before any database write occurs
The service layer raises a rejection error when a write would result in a stored quantity below zero (overcommitting write), before any database write occurs
A validation error response from the boundary includes the name of the specific offending field rather than a generic error message
Integration tests connect to the real branch database via DATABASE_URL with no mock or in-memory driver present
Filing a stock record with a uuid-suffixed SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code results in that record being durably persisted and retrievable via the API
Rendering <App> inside <MemoryRouter initialEntries={["/stock/file"]}> mounts the stock-filing page at route /stock/file
The stock-filing form on /stock/file carries the design-guide seam attribute data-testid="stock-file-form"
The SKU input on the filing form carries data-testid="sku-input"
The location input on the filing form carries data-testid="location-input"
The quantity input on the filing form carries data-testid="quantity-input"
The inventory_code input on the filing form carries data-testid="inventory-code-input"
After a successful file submission the element carrying data-testid="file-success" becomes visible on the filing page
The boundary layer (app/routes/) returns JSON responses and contains no server-side template rendering
Retrieved stock record returns the exact quantity and combined inventory_code that were previously filed via the API
Rendering <App> inside <MemoryRouter initialEntries={["/stock"]}> mounts the stock record view at route /stock
The quantity display on the stock record view carries data-testid="stock-quantity"
The inventory_code display on the stock record view carries data-testid="stock-inventory-code"
Inserting two rows with the same (sku, location) pair raises a unique-constraint violation on the real branch database, verifying the composite unique constraint
The read-then-write upsert for an existing (sku, location) pair executes within a single database transaction so a concurrent repeat write cannot produce two rows
The created_at timestamp on a stock_records row is unchanged after an in-place upsert updates that row for the same (sku, location) pair
Filing stock for an existing uuid-suffixed (sku, location) pair updates the record in place so exactly one row exists with the new values and no error is returned
After submitting the filing form for an already-existing SKU-location pair through <App> at /stock/file, no element with data-testid="file-error" is present in the DOM
After a collision-path submission through <App> at /stock/file the element carrying data-testid="file-success" is visible, confirming success feedback is shown rather than an error state
